newsitem.title: USA: Lobbyist testifies about Rep. Burton, fund-raising.
newsitem.headline: Lobbyist testifies about Rep. Burton, fund-raising.

text.p: A lobbyist testified before a federal grand jury Wednesday about allegations that Representative Dan Burton, a Republican leading a House investigaion into campaign fund-raising abuses, had shaken him down for contributions.

Lobbyist Mark Siegel spent nearly three hours before the grand jury, which previously focused on the campaign fund-raising controversy involving the Democrats, President Clinton and Vice President Al Gore.
As Siegel left the U.S. courthouse afterward, his attorney, Plato Cacheris, told reporters the testimony "involves fund-raising activities by Mr. Burton, congressman from Indiana."

Siegel, a former lobbyist for the Pakistan government, has alleged Burton threatened him with the loss of business if he did not raise at least $5,000 from Pakistani-Americans for the lawmaker's re-election campaign last year.
Siegel, a longtime Democratic activist, alleged in a two-page memo in July that he had been "shaken down" by Burton.

After Siegel said he could not raise the money, he alleged that "Burton threatened me and has now obviously attempted to interfere with my livelihood" by contacting Pakistani officials to express his anger.
Cacheris said: "You can assume the whole subject of the testimony was about the matters that have been reported in the press. We're not going to discuss any particulars."
Burton, chairman of a House committee investigating campaign finance abuses, has denied the allegations as "baloney." Asked about Burton's comment, Cacheris replied, "That's baloney."

He said Siegel has not had any recent conversations with Burton and does not plan any. Also testifying before the grand jury was Siegel's business associate, Brian Sailer, who has corroborated Siegel's account.

The grand jury, which has been investigating potential campaign law violations, is hearing evidence as part of its secret proceedings and will decide whether to bring any charges. The panel is being directed by a Justice Department task force of prosecutors probing campaign fund-raising.
